The level qualifier protects nothing: the phases section is level-independent. plan.md.tmpl guards content with <!-- IF level:... --> at :1, :4, :7, :10, :13, :16, :97, :203 and :286, but ## 4. IMPLEMENTATION PHASES at :123 sits between the ANCHOR:phases marker at :122 and its close at :127 with no guard, while ## 5. TESTING STRATEGY at :132 is guarded twice in the same file (:135 level 1, :138 levels 2/3/3+). Corpus heading presence tracks level barely at all: Level 1 96.6% (1667/1725), Level 2 96.2% (2380/2474), Level 3 93.4% (596/638), Level 3+ 90.6% (29/32). create.sh:322-324 states the reason: 'Core templates (~270 LOC) are shared across all levels.' Iteration 2's finding 12 requirement for a level qualifier is withdrawn.

plan.md is a Level 1 required document, listed in folder-structure.md's Level 1 Required Files directly after spec.md and before tasks.md; acceptance-criteria.md is the only file the level contract withholds from Level 1. A rule about the plan's shape therefore cannot be a Level 2 and above rule.

The strict phase predicate is a new obligation, not the enforcement of existing practice, so the validator backstop half of the recommendation is withdrawn. Running iteration 7's predicate (three lines inside ## 4. IMPLEMENTATION PHASES, each holding a backticked token and a Verify: clause with a command) over 4915 git-tracked plan.md files returns exactly 1 pass. Loosened to 'at least three body lines under the heading' the figure is 68.3% (3359), and 'the section names Setup, Implementation and Verification somewhere' is 66.0% (3242). A rule for the path-plus-proof shape would fail 4914 packets on the day it landed, and a creation-date cutoff would police a behaviour nothing has ever produced.

Contradictory evidence, resolved: iteration 7's retroactivity radius was inflated about 5x by a denominator that included gitignored files. Iteration 7 reported 4677 of 6098 = 76.7%; tracked denominators give 4692 of 4915 = 95.5%, i.e. 223 packets missing the heading (4.5%, not 23%). The numerators agree within 15 files; the denominators differ by 1183, which is exactly the population find sees and rg -l does not because rg honours .gitignore. Sampling 400 of those 1183 through git check-ignore --stdin returned 400 of 400 ignored. The tracked denominator prevails because the rule a validator applies runs in CI over tracked files.

The authoring card and the plan template contradict each other about where the phases live, and the template wins because it is in the file. Card :113 says the plan 'names its three phases, Setup, Implementation and Verification, one line each, under ## 4. IMPLEMENTATION PHASES'. Template :126, in the body of that same section, says 'Follow the ordered tasks in tasks.md. It owns the Setup, Implementation and Verification phase checkboxes and task state.' A session reading the scaffolded file is told the phases are tasks.md's business. This is the mechanism behind finding 3's 1-in-4915 adoption, and it is why the edit set must reach the template and not only the card.

Final recommendation: six amended lines across three existing files, zero new files. AGENTS.md is 27372 bytes; the 16384-byte injection window ends 1061 bytes past the start of :176 and :176 occupies 135 bytes, leaving 926 bytes for a bullet placed after it; the draft bullet measures 291 bytes. The six lines are card :113 (decidable shape, no level qualifier), card :120 (worked example brought into compliance; it currently returns zero predicate matches), card :123-124 (acceptance matched to the amended rule, verify naming IMPLEMENTATION PHASES rather than the number 4), template :124 (fill note teaches path-plus-proof), template :126 (tasks.md ownership clause qualified), and the AGENTS.md bullet. Two targets dropped since iteration 7: the level qualifier clause and the new validator script plus registry entry.
The phases section must stay unguarded by level in plan.md.tmpl, or the card's rule and the template's structure diverge as they did before this iteration
The AGENTS.md addition must not exceed 926 bytes and must not reinstate a review-verdict clause
The card's verify must name the IMPLEMENTATION PHASES heading, never the section number 4, or it passes on a plan with no phases section

direction: Keeping the level qualifier out of caution
reason: The phases section is unguarded in the template at every level and Level 1 requires plan.md, so the clause would exempt a packet class that already carries the heading 96.6% of the time. A clause that changes nothing on the scaffolded path is dead text in a section whose problem is that it says too much and disagrees with itself.

direction: Taking the backstop with a creation-date cutoff following AC_CLOSURE's dated-scoping precedent
reason: folder-structure.md:156 shows the mechanism exists and works, but a dated cutoff suits a rule whose subject is universally present and newly required; the path-plus-proof line is present in 1 of 4915 packets, so the cutoff would police a behaviour nothing has ever produced while the prose that would produce it is the thing being shipped.

direction: Fixing the card alone and leaving the template's tasks.md ownership clause in place
reason: The contradiction is bidirectional; amending one side leaves the scaffolded file instructing the opposite of the reference, and the template is the half that reaches sessions which never open the card.

direction: Using description.json's level as a reliable corpus join key
reason: It works for 4915 tracked packets, but 38 carry level 'unset' and 6 have no description, and those residue classes sit at 47.4% and 33.3% heading presence. A future measurement should report the unjoined residue rather than fold it into the denominator, which is the same error f-iter008-004 corrects.
